4: (a) It was clear that many candidates were not familiar with the term. Many understood that it had objectives other than profit or identified what these other objectives might include. Only the strongest answers were able to give a precise definition. (b) Well answered. (c) Most candidates could identify at least one stakeholder group. Candidates who did well were then able to explain why stakeholder groups such as ‘banks’ and ‘the local community’ might be interested in this business. Application in many responses was limited or not attempted. (d) Most candidates were able to identify one factor with low revenue being the typical issue. Better responses attempted to explain why each factor needed to be considered. Only the best responses linked their answer to the scenario. Instead of development, weaker responses just repeated the knowledge point or simply offered the same explanation for both reasons. (e) Good knowledge of methods was evident in most responses. Better responses developed the points made and also used the information from the stem to help support the final decision made. Weaker answers listed different methods rather than explain how these methods might be appropriate. Evaluation in most responses was simple or not attempted. BUSINESS STUDIES
